name: VQE Chemistry Benchmark
description: Quantum chemistry is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers in the near future. For noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices, the quantum-classical hybrid framework based on the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) has become the method of choice. In the literature, there are many different variants of VQE, but it is not known which one is optimal for a given molecule. For this purpose, we perform a thorough benchmarking on more than ten different kinds of VQE ansatzes (in systems up to 30 qubits), based on their performance on the energy accuracy, runtime until convergence, and number of parameters. Our results show that the ADAPT ansatz can be used to obtain more accurate energy for small systems (below 14 qubits), but it costs much more computational resources. For larger molecules, UCCSD0 has better performance. However, all the tested ansatzes can hardly reach chemical accuracy at stretched bond lengths. typical_sota_score: chemical accuracy is often not reached; best results are typically near chemical accuracy for small systems and worse for larger or stretched-bond cases
reputation: A useful comparative benchmark for VQE ansatz design in quantum chemistry, but it is a specialized research benchmark rather than a broadly standardized community leaderboard.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; performance depends strongly on molecule size, ansatz choice, and bond geometry, and stretched bond lengths remain especially challenging.
